record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.context_brief: long rational cycles over number fields
record.original_question: Over a number field K, can one construct infinite families of generalized Hénon maps of algebraic degree d having K-rational cycles of length at least d+3? More strongly, can one get maps with N_d periodic points where N_d−d→∞, or even N_d/d→∞, as d→∞?

evidence.quote: Question 45. — Over a number field K, is it possible to construct infinite families of generalized Hénon maps of algebraic degree d, and K-rational cycles of length at least d + 3? Can one construct maps with Nd periodic points, where Nd − d → ∞, or even Nd/d → ∞ as d → ∞?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let K be a number field. A generalized Hénon map of algebraic degree d ≥ 2 is an automorphism of the affine plane A^2 obtained as a finite composition of maps of "shear" form, namely maps (x, y) ↦ (y, p(y) − a x) with a ∈ K* and p ∈ K[y] of degree d (more generally, finite compositions of such generalized shears whose Jacobian determinant is a nonzero constant). For such a map f defined over K, write Per(f, K) for the set of K-rational periodic points of f, let N_d = N_d(f) = |Per(f, K)|, and call a K-rational cycle of f a finite orbit of f consisting entirely of K-rational points; its length is its cardinality.

(a) Does there exist, for some number field K, an infinite family of generalized Hénon maps {f_d}, with f_d of algebraic degree d (defined over K), such that f_d possesses a K-rational cycle of length at least d + 3?

(b) Stronger: can one produce such a family with N_d − d → ∞ as d → ∞?

(c) Stronger still: can one produce such a family with N_d / d → ∞ as d → ∞?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Kim, Krieger, Postolache, Szeto, 2024) constructs, for each odd integer d ≥ 2, a Hénon map of degree d defined over ℚ admitting at least (d − 4)² integral periodic points, and explicitly states their examples also admit integer cycles of large period. This implies N_d/d → ∞ over K = ℚ, settling the strongest asymptotic form (c) (and hence (b)) affirmatively over ℚ. Whether one can simultaneously achieve a single K-rational cycle of length ≥ d + 3 for an infinite family is not explicitly claimed in the abstract; the precise length-versus-degree question (a) appears at most partially addressed.

status_evidence.title: Hénon maps with many rational periodic points
status_evidence.snippet: For each odd integer d ≥ 2 we produce a Hénon map of degree d defined over ℚ with at least (d − 4)^2 integral periodic points... our examples also admit integer cycles of large period.
status_evidence.claim: Provides Hénon maps over ℚ with quadratically many rational periodic points and long integer cycles, addressing parts (b)–(c) of the question over ℚ.
